finding.text: Ask 2 (each sentence appears live as its words arrive) is not built: `ext/Refine/doc/session-log-2026-10-10.md:16` lists it under "Not built yet". It is an ask the owner named, so either build the interim `clean` lines with `final:false` that the doc plans, or split it into its own task and card so it is not lost.

The raw stage's `source` is always "typed": `RefineSystem.js:79` sends `this.source ?? "typed"`, but nothing in the diff ever sets `RefineSystem.source`. That holds even for dictated prompts, which are the case this task is about. Set it to "dictated" when the text came from `ux/Dictate`/Whisper.

The browser cannot find the log the server writes. On a first write, node's `PromptLog.add` → `AISession.locate` (`core/Session/Session.js:53-57`) makes `./<day>/session-<8 chars>/`, but the browser's `PromptLog.read` → `AISession.dir_url(id)` (`Session.js:20`) falls back to the flat `./<id>/` path, because the browser has no `days`/`slugs` entry for this made-up demo uuid. So the "open the session" link (`Prompt.js:384`) likely opens an empty or 404 session page. Check it against the running site and fix the path; the headless test fakes `/api/refine`, so it never checks this.

The folder never says which session it belongs to: `scan()` (`Session.js:22-23`) only finds a session's id in `index.json`, the cache summary or `page.jsonl`, and the new folder has none of them, only `prompts.jsonl`. After a Servex restart on a later day, `locate` makes a second folder for the same session. Writing an `index.json` with the id the first time would fix it.

`PromptLog.add` (`PromptLog.js:167-174`) reads the file, checks it, then appends, with no lock. Two refines on the same session at once could both pass the "raw is immutable" check. Prompt ids are fresh per request, so the risk is small, but `prompt` is taken from the request body (`run.js:86`), so a client could reuse one.

`Annotator.BATCH_CHARS = 60000` (`Annotator.js:24`) can never split a batch, because `run_refine` already refuses text over 20000 characters (`run.js:82`). The batching code could go until longer inputs exist (less is more), or the cap could match the real limit.

Good reuse: `Outline.js` takes the parser out of `Prompt.js` so the browser and Servex share one copy (law 6). The headless test covers the notes display and replaying a saved log. Echo is untouched, as asked.

The session folder is named `session-xxxxxxxx`, not by its uuid, so it is lost after a restart. In `public/framework/ai/AISession/PromptLog.js:167`, `add()` calls `read()` → `AISession.read_text` → `locate(id)` without a slug before line 171 runs `locate(id, undefined, id)`, and `core/Session/Session.js:56` has already stored the default slug by then. The folder ends up holding only `prompts.jsonl` (no uuid name, no index.json, no cache.jsonl, no page.jsonl), so `Session.scan()` (Session.js:31-35) never finds it again. After a Servex restart, or on another day, reads come back empty, the "raw is immutable" and "write the raw line first" checks pass against nothing, and the browser's "open the session" link (`Prompt.js` ~line 384) points at a folder it can't resolve. Fix: call `locate(id, undefined, id)` once at the top of `add()` before reading, or have `read_text` pass the slug through.

Ask 2 (live per sentence) is not delivered to the log: `run.js` writes `raw` only after the whole text arrives, then one `clean` with `final:true`. The doc admits this (`doc/session-log-2026-10-10.md:460`, "Not built yet: per-sentence streaming"). The page's existing `load_quick` path shows the instant clean, but nothing streams into `prompts.jsonl` or gets tailed with `live()`. Either build the interim `final:false` clean lines, or say clearly on the task card that ask 2 is deferred.

Only the Refine demo page writes a log, and it does so under a made-up per-browser uuid (`RefineSystem.js:419-425`), not the Claude session the owner is dictating into. The requirement says "the session's own log", so this is a stand-in until VS Code prompts are wired. Worth one line on the card.

`Annotator.batches` (`Servex/ext/refine/Annotator.js:33-42`) can never make more than one batch: `run.js:82` already caps text at 20,000 characters, and `BATCH_CHARS` is 60,000. A single call would be simpler. Also, the comment on line 18 ("about 15k tokens") describes 60k characters, which is correct but easy to misread as a 15k-character cap.

`Annotator.annotate` swallows every error (`Annotator.js:56`, `catch { return []; }`). A Haiku failure then logs a `notes` line with empty alternates, names and tags, and gives no sign in `log_errors`. Surfacing the error would make a broken Haiku pass visible.

`PromptLog.add` re-reads and folds the whole `prompts.jsonl` on every append (`PromptLog.js:167`). That is fine at today's size, but it is O(n) per line for a session holding hundreds of prompts, and it is not safe if two writers append to the same prompt at once.

Good: Echo is untouched, cites are stored 0-based and shown 1-based consistently (`Outline.indexes` / `Prompt.from_log`), `parse_outline` moved into one shared `Outline` class rather than being copied, and `test/session-log.mjs` covers the request, the notes view and the replay.
